_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When a commit touches that audit's `Code paths` afterwards, the
check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> set
`reviewedAt` to the SHA you reviewed through and say why in `note`.
What is NOT legitimate is bumping `reviewedAt` without reading the diff.
The note is the evidence that someone did.

docs/IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md.note: Two commits of drift, neither moves a §1-§5 claim. (a) cad05cb is the squash-merge of the very PR that produced revision 1.3; its `Audited commit` records the pre-squash branch SHA 3ff0c78, which is a real object but not an ancestor of main, so the gate cannot see that the two are the same code. Under the audited paths cad05cb touches only SubjectNormalizer.java — the B1-2 fix §4b already describes. (b) defb756 changes which exception MailConnectionProbe throws when the server rejects a login: MailAuthenticationException instead of MailConnectionException, so the reply text stops being rendered into the user-facing error.mail.connectionFailed placeholder and travels as the cause into the log instead. That narrows what server-controlled text reaches the UI; it touches no TLS, auth-mechanism or timeout setting. Re-checked on the probe specifically: pinned ssl.checkserveridentity, the fail-closed OAuth2-requires-SSL guard and the millisecond-string timeouts are all unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.
